What If a Star Exploded So Bright You Could See It in Daylight?

In the year 1006, a supernova appeared that was bright enough to see during the day and to read by at night. People recorded it in China, Japan, Egypt and Europe.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

#supernova #space #history #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: A thousand years ago, a star exploded so brightly, people could see it in broad daylight.
It happened in the year one thousand and six. A new star suddenly appeared in the southern sky.
It was the brightest star-like event in recorded history, far brighter than Venus.
Some reports say it was bright enough to read by at night. And it stayed visible for months.
segments.headline: Visible for months

segments.text: People wrote about it in China, Japan, Egypt and Europe. A doctor in Cairo said it was three times bigger than Venus.
segments.headline: Seen around the world

segments.text: It was a white dwarf star that exploded about seven thousand light-years away.
Today, telescopes can still see the expanding cloud it left behind.
segments.headline: Still expanding
